questions.q: A patient requests removal of a red and orange decorative tattoo. Which Q-switched laser wavelength preferentially targets red/orange ink via complementary colour absorption?
opts: Q-switched Nd:YAG 1064 nm — targets black and dark blue tattoo ink
Q-switched alexandrite 755 nm — targets blue, green, and black tattoo ink
Q-switched frequency-doubled Nd:YAG 532 nm — targets red and orange tattoo ink via complementary colour absorption
Q-switched ruby 694 nm — targets blue, green, and black tattoo ink
questions.exp: Laser tattoo removal uses selective chromophore absorption: red/orange ink absorbs green light (complementary colour). The 532 nm wavelength (green) is preferentially absorbed by red and orange pigments. 1064 nm targets black/dark blue; 694 nm (ruby) and 755 nm (alexandrite) target blue/green/black. Choosing the correct wavelength per ink colour is critical for efficacy and to avoid paradoxical darkening of flesh-coloured/white inks.

questions.q: Cytotoxic chemotherapy causes anagen effluvium by which mechanism, and how does onset timing differ from telogen effluvium?
opts: Direct cytotoxic damage to rapidly proliferating matrix keratinocytes causes hair shaft fracture (Pohl-Pinkus constriction) and shedding within 2–4 weeks — far earlier than telogen effluvium's 3-month lag
Immune-mediated peribulbar lymphocytic attack identical to alopecia areata, triggered by chemotherapy metabolites acting as neo-antigens
Telomere shortening in matrix cells after repeated cycles induces premature replicative senescence and arrest of hair growth
Hormonal disruption by chemotherapy metabolites activating androgen receptors in dermal papilla cells, triggering premature catagen
questions.exp: Chemotherapy agents (alkylating agents, taxanes, anthracyclines) are cytotoxic to the most rapidly dividing cells in the body — the hair matrix keratinocytes in anagen follicles. Abrupt arrest of hair shaft production causes the shaft to narrow and fracture (Pohl-Pinkus constriction), with shedding 2–4 weeks after treatment onset. This is far earlier than telogen effluvium (3-month lag after trigger). Hair regrows after treatment, sometimes with temporary changes in texture and colour.

questions.q: Frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA) is distinguished from androgenetic alopecia (AGA) at the frontal hairline on trichoscopy by:
opts: Increased single-hair follicular units and >20% hair diameter variability (anisotrichosis) indicating follicular miniaturisation
Diffuse yellow dots and black dots reflecting sebaceous hyperplasia and follicular dropout
Exclamation mark hairs and Pohl-Pinkus constrictions indicating active lymphocytic matrix attack
Peripilar erythema, tubular peripilar casts (sleeve-like scale around follicle openings), absent follicular ostia in scarred zones, and frequent eyebrow and eyelash loss
questions.exp: FFA trichoscopy: peripilar erythema and tubular/sleeve-like peripilar casts at the active margin, with complete absence of follicular ostia in the scarred zone, distinguish it from AGA (which shows anisotrichosis and peripilar halos but no follicular dropout or casts). Eyebrow loss (50–80% of FFA patients) and body hair recession are characteristic. AGA shows miniaturisation without inflammation or scarring.

questions.q: Liquid nitrogen cryotherapy for actinic keratoses destroys dysplastic keratinocytes by:
opts: Selective photothermolysis of dysplastic keratinocytes due to abnormal melanin deposition in AKs absorbing the nitrogen's radiation
Intracellular ice crystal formation causing membrane rupture, plus extracellular ice formation causing vascular stasis and ischaemic cell death during the freeze-thaw cycle
Osmotic cellular death from the hyperosmolar extracellular environment created during tissue freezing
Photodynamic generation of reactive oxygen species from UV radiation reflected by the ice crystals activating endogenous porphyrins
questions.exp: Liquid nitrogen (−196°C) destroys cells via: (1) rapid freeze → intracellular ice crystal formation → membrane and organelle rupture; (2) slow thaw → recrystallisation → additional cell injury; (3) vascular stasis from endothelial damage → ischaemic necrosis. A 5-second freeze producing a 1–2 mm ice halo around the AK is the standard clinical endpoint. A double freeze-thaw cycle increases cell kill for thicker lesions.

questions.q: Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB, 311 nm) is preferred over PUVA for vitiligo phototherapy because:
opts: NB-UVB requires no photosensitiser, avoids PUVA-related risks (GI side effects, cataract risk, long-term carcinogenicity), achieves comparable repigmentation, and is safe in children and pregnancy
NB-UVB penetrates more deeply, reaching dermal melanocyte stem cells in the hair follicle bulge more effectively than PUVA's longer wavelengths
NB-UVB specifically activates MC1R on melanocyte progenitors, while PUVA only induces migration of existing mature melanocytes
NB-UVB has a higher minimal erythema dose (MED) than PUVA, allowing higher absolute fluences and faster repigmentation per session
questions.exp: NB-UVB is first-line phototherapy for vitiligo. Advantages over PUVA: no oral psoralen required (avoids nausea, hepatotoxicity, mandatory post-treatment UV eye protection for 24 h, long-term melanoma risk). Repigmentation rates are comparable. NB-UVB works via immunosuppression (reducing T-cell attack on melanocytes) and stimulating follicular melanocyte reservoir migration. Safe in children and during pregnancy, unlike PUVA (teratogenic psoralens).

questions.q: Profhilo (stabilised HA 64 mg/2 mL) differs from conventional volumising HA dermal fillers because:
opts: It contains high molecular weight HA with the highest BDDE cross-linking density of any injectable HA, producing the longest-lasting volumising effect
It is injected subdermally at 5 Bio-Aesthetic Points (BAP) per side and acts primarily as a mid-face volumiser for structural support
It contains uncrosslinked hybrid H-HA/L-HA complexes that bioremodel the dermis — stimulating collagen types I, III, IV and elastin — without adding significant volume
It contains methylene blue as a photosensitiser for optional light-activated enhancement of dermal remodelling
questions.exp: Profhilo contains hybrid cooperative complexes of uncrosslinked high MW HA (1100 kDa) + low MW HA (80 kDa) with no BDDE crosslinker. Unlike volumising fillers, it has minimal filling effect. High HA concentration stimulates fibroblasts to produce collagen types I, III, IV and elastin (bioremodelling), improving skin laxity, hydration, and quality. Injected at 5 BAP points per side. Results: improved skin quality — not structural volume — lasting ~6 months, requiring 2 sessions 4 weeks apart.

questions.q: When injecting HA filler for lip augmentation, the 'white roll' that defines lip border definition refers to:
opts: The vermillion — the red/pink pigmented mucosal zone between the dry lip and the wet labial mucosa
Cupid's bow — the double-curved upper vermillion border creating two peaks and a central trough at the midline
The philtral columns — the paired vertical ridges descending from the nasal base to the Cupid's bow peaks
The vermillion border — the raised mucocutaneous ridge at the skin-to-vermillion junction on the upper lip, which defines lip shape and is the primary target for border restoration with filler
questions.exp: Lip anatomy: the white roll is the slightly elevated, pale skin ridge immediately above the vermillion border on the upper lip — the mucocutaneous junction between the cutaneous (skin) lip and the vermillion. It defines lip border sharpness and 'pout.' HA filler injected along the vermillion border restores or enhances the white roll. Injecting too superficially into the white roll risks the Tyndall effect; too deep loses border definition.

questions.q: Fractional RF microneedling (e.g., Morpheus8) is preferred over fractional ablative CO₂ laser for patients with Fitzpatrick skin types IV–VI because:
opts: Fractional RF penetrates more deeply than fractional CO₂, reaching subcutaneous fat for full-face rejuvenation in a single session
Fractional RF delivers energy directly into the dermis via insulated microneedles, bypassing the epidermis — dramatically reducing epidermal melanocyte stimulation and PIH risk in dark skin types
Fractional RF is more effective for superficial photorejuvenation and lentigines because radiofrequency specifically targets UV-damaged keratinocytes
Fractional RF has zero downtime compared to fractional CO₂ which causes 7–14 days of open wound healing in all skin types
questions.exp: In fractional RF microneedling, insulated needles (coated except at the tips) deliver RF energy directly to the dermis at the needle tip, without heating the epidermis. This largely bypasses epidermal melanocytes, dramatically reducing PIH risk in FST IV–VI — the primary barrier to using fractional ablative lasers in darker skin. Energy delivery depth (1.5–4 mm) is adjustable. Downtime is 1–3 days (erythema) vs. 7–14 days for fractional CO₂.

questions.q: Telangiectatic matting (TM) is a complication of sclerotherapy. It refers to:
opts: Development of new fine red telangiectasias (<0.2 mm) around the treated vessels, caused by VEGF upregulation from local hypoxia following sclerosant-induced occlusion
Recanalisation of the treated varicosity with new varicose tributaries developing in the same distribution as the original vessels
Permanent haemosiderin-induced hyperpigmentation along the treated vessel track from extravasated erythrocytes
Allergic contact dermatitis to the sclerosant producing an erythematous reticular pattern around injection sites
questions.exp: Telangiectatic matting = new fine red telangiectasias (<0.2 mm) forming around the sclerotherapy treatment area. Mechanism: sclerosant-induced vessel occlusion → local hypoxia → upregulation of VEGF and angiogenic factors → neovascularisation. Risk factors: high sclerosant concentration, large volumes per session, obesity, oestrogen therapy. Most cases resolve within 3–12 months. Persistent TM may respond to low-fluence PDL or nd:YAG laser.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman develops excessive terminal hair on the upper lip, chin, chest, and central abdomen. Total testosterone is elevated at 3.5 nmol/L. This is correctly classified as:
opts: Hypertrichosis — generalised excess hair growth in a non-androgen-dependent distribution
Congenital hypertrichosis lanuginosa — diffuse lanugo hair retention from birth, not androgen-dependent

Hirsutism — androgen-dependent terminal hair growth in a male-pattern distribution in a woman, with elevated androgens requiring investigation for PCOS, adrenal hyperplasia, or androgen-secreting tumour
Hypertrichosis universalis acquisita — caused by cyclosporin or phenytoin driving diffuse vellus hair proliferation
questions.exp: Hirsutism = androgen-dependent terminal hair growth in Ferriman-Gallwey distribution (upper lip, chin, chest, upper abdomen, inner thighs) in women. Total testosterone >3.0 nmol/L signals a pathological cause requiring investigation: PCOS (most common), late-onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), androgen-secreting ovarian/adrenal tumour. Hypertrichosis is generalised hair excess independent of androgen stimulation, any body site, any gender — drug or systemic disease driven.

questions.q: What correctly distinguishes galvanic electrolysis from thermolysis (short-wave diathermy) for permanent hair removal?
opts: Both use DC current at different voltages to generate sodium hydroxide at the needle tip, with galvanic using lower voltage than thermolysis
Galvanic uses AC high-frequency current to generate heat; thermolysis uses DC current to produce chemical lye (NaOH)
Thermolysis uses DC current with heat generated at 500 kHz; galvanic uses AC current producing NaOH via electrolysis

Galvanic uses DC current producing NaOH (lye) via electrolysis of tissue fluid causing chemical follicular destruction; thermolysis uses high-frequency AC current (500 kHz–13 MHz) generating localised heat to thermally coagulate follicular cells; the blend method combines both
questions.exp: Galvanic electrolysis: DC current causes electrolysis of tissue saline → produces NaOH (lye) at the needle cathode → chemical destruction of follicular cells. Slow (1–3 min/hair) but thorough. Thermolysis (short-wave diathermy): high-frequency AC (500 kHz–13 MHz) creates rapid oscillating molecular vibration → localised heat at needle tip → thermal coagulation. Faster (seconds/hair). Blend combines chemical + thermal destruction for difficult follicles. All three are FDA-cleared for permanent hair removal.

questions.q: Botulinum toxin injection into the masseter for jaw slimming (masseteric hypertrophy) reduces lower facial width by:
opts: Causing disuse atrophy of masseter muscle fibres over 3–6 months from reduced neuromuscular activity; repeated injections every 4–6 months required; dose 20–40 U onabotulinumtoxinA per masseter per session
Directly inhibiting masseter fibroblast collagen production, reducing the connective tissue framework maintaining masseteric bulk
Reducing parotid gland secretory mass and volume, contributing to lower facial width reduction over time
Inducing caspase-mediated myofibre apoptosis through acetylcholine accumulation at the paralysed neuromuscular junction
questions.exp: Botox paralyses the masseter → progressive disuse atrophy as myosin heavy chain isoforms switch and myofibres reduce cross-sectional area over 3–6 months. Repeated injections every 4–6 months are required; after prolonged treatment, results may last longer due to cumulative atrophy. Dose: 20–40 U onabotulinumtoxinA per masseter. Injection too superiorly risks zygomaticus major involvement → lip elevation weakness ('chipmunk' asymmetry).

questions.q: Trichorrhexis nodosa (TN) on light microscopy shows which pathognomonic appearance?
opts: Regular beaded narrowings alternating with wider nodular segments (monilethrix) — from a structural keratin gene defect
Focal cortical fraying at nodal points resembling two opposing interlocking paint brushes, caused by physical/chemical trauma or amino acid metabolism defects
Longitudinal splitting from the distal hair shaft end (trichoptilosis/split ends), with no discrete nodal points on the shaft
Twisting of the hair shaft on its own axis at irregular 180° intervals (pili torti) associated with Menkes kinky hair syndrome
questions.exp: Trichorrhexis nodosa: the hair shaft cortex frays at focal weak points (nodes), creating a brushed appearance — two opposing paint brushes meeting at the fracture site on microscopy. Acquired causes: excessive bleaching, chemical relaxing, heat, friction. Congenital causes: argininosuccinic aciduria, trichothiodystrophy, Netherton syndrome (associated with SPINK5 mutations). Monilethrix shows alternating elliptical nodes and intermittent narrowings (constrictions). Pili torti = shaft twisted on its axis.

questions.q: The Obagi Blue Peel uses TCA combined with a blue glycerin base. The primary purpose of the blue base is:
opts: The blue pigment acts as a photosensitiser, enhancing TCA penetration when treated skin is exposed to visible light post-application
The blue indicator changes colour to green-yellow when TCA reaches the papillary dermis, providing a chemical endpoint for peel depth
The blue glycerin/saponin base retards TCA absorption rate, controlling penetration depth and ensuring uniform coverage; the blue dye provides visual contrast to track which areas have been treated
Methylene blue in the base has antimicrobial properties preventing post-peel colonisation of the disrupted stratum corneum
questions.exp: The Obagi Blue Peel base contains glycerin and saponins that slow TCA absorption into skin, allowing controlled and more uniform penetration depth. The blue dye (indigo carmine) provides visual contrast so the applicator can track which areas of the face have been covered evenly, preventing missed zones or double-application. This controlled delivery allows TCA to be used more safely by less experienced practitioners. The blue dye washes off during initial exfoliation.

questions.q: White tattoo ink is the most difficult to remove with Q-switched lasers because:
opts: White ink (TiO₂) absorbs equally across all visible wavelengths, preventing selective targeting by any single laser wavelength
White ink particles are too large (>100 μm) for photoacoustic fragmentation by nanosecond or picosecond laser pulses
White ink is deposited in the deep reticular dermis beyond the optical penetration depth of Q-switched laser systems
White ink (TiO₂/ZnO) paradoxically darkens to grey-black after laser irradiation due to photoreduction of Ti⁴⁺ (white) to Ti³⁺ (dark grey), making subsequent sessions significantly more difficult
questions.exp: TiO₂-based white/flesh-coloured ink is poorly absorbed by Q-switched laser wavelengths and — critically — undergoes photoreduction on laser irradiation: Ti⁴⁺ (white) is reduced to Ti³⁺ (dark grey-black), paradoxically darkening the treated area. This darkened ink is harder to remove in subsequent laser sessions. A test spot should always be performed before treating white or flesh-coloured ink. Complete removal is often unachievable.

questions.q: Following microneedling-induced platelet activation, which growth factor is released FIRST from platelet alpha-granules to initiate dermal fibroblast recruitment?
opts: Platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) — the primary chemotactic signal recruiting fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells; followed by TGF-β (collagen synthesis), VEGF (angiogenesis), and EGF (epithelialisation)
TGF-β1 — the primary fibroblast activator, released before PDGF to directly upregulate procollagen synthesis at the wound site
VEGF — establishes neovascularisation first, supplying oxygen before fibroblast recruitment and collagen synthesis can proceed
EGF — initiates keratinocyte proliferation which then releases paracrine signals to recruit dermal fibroblasts
questions.exp: Post-injury growth factor cascade: PDGF is the primary early-release chemotactic signal from platelet alpha-granules, driving fibroblast and smooth muscle cell migration to the wound. TGF-β1/2 follows, upregulating procollagen I/III synthesis and suppressing collagenase. VEGF drives angiogenesis. EGF and FGF promote keratinocyte proliferation. TGF-β3 promotes scarless healing. This sequence underpins both PRP therapy and microneedling-induced collagen induction therapy.

questions.q: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is preferred over titanium dioxide (TiO₂) as a single inorganic UV filter for broad-spectrum protection because:
opts: ZnO has superior water resistance and substantivity, making it more durable during aqueous or sweat-exposed conditions

ZnO provides broader UVA coverage than TiO₂ — absorbing across both UVA2 (315–340 nm) AND UVA1 (340–400 nm), while TiO₂ has reduced absorption in UVA1; ZnO also generates fewer reactive oxygen species on UV exposure
ZnO nanoparticles penetrate the stratum corneum less deeply than TiO₂, reducing systemic absorption and improving safety
ZnO is more cosmetically elegant with less white cast than TiO₂ at equivalent concentrations due to its higher refractive index
questions.exp: ZnO absorbs across UVB (280–315 nm), UVA2 (315–340 nm), and UVA1 (340–400 nm) — making it the broadest-spectrum single inorganic filter. TiO₂ absorbs UVB and UVA2 well but has significantly reduced absorption above 340 nm (UVA1 gap). ZnO also generates fewer reactive oxygen species (ROS) on UV exposure compared to TiO₂. Both reflect/scatter UV physically (not photochemically). Nanoparticle forms (<100 nm) of both reduce cosmetic white cast.

questions.q: Lichen planopilaris (LPP) and FFA share the same underlying pathology. On trichoscopy, LPP at the scalp vertex is distinguished from AGA by:
opts: Yellow dots and black dots indicating follicular miniaturisation and cadaverised hairs — characteristic of AGA and alopecia areata
Exclamation mark hairs and Pohl-Pinkus constrictions indicating active lymphocytic attack on anagen bulbs

Perifollicular erythema, peripilar casts (tubular white scale adherent around follicle openings), and absent follicular ostia in scarred zones — same findings as FFA but at vertex/crown rather than frontal hairline
Honeycomb pigmentation between follicles indicating interfollicular epidermal dermis involvement
questions.exp: LPP and FFA are variants of the same entity (lymphocytic cicatricial alopecia targeting the follicular isthmus/infundibulum) with identical trichoscopy: peripilar erythema, peripilar casts (tubular scale), and absent follicular ostia in scarred zones. LPP affects vertex/parietal scalp; FFA affects frontotemporal hairline. Both produce irreversible scarring. Treatment: hydroxychloroquine, doxycycline, topical/intralesional corticosteroids. Biopsy shows perifollicular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate at the infundibulum.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with multiple solar lentigines on the dorsum of the hands requests laser treatment. The most appropriate laser is:
opts: Q-switched frequency-doubled Nd:YAG 532 nm — targets superficial epidermal melanin with high absorption at this wavelength; appropriate for epidermal pigmented lesions in FST I–III
Long-pulsed Nd:YAG 1064 nm — provides deeper dermal penetration to reach lentigo pigment deposited in the upper papillary dermis
Q-switched ruby 694 nm — specifically targets lentigo melanin with less risk of surrounding epidermal injury than 532 nm
Er:YAG 2940 nm — ablates pigment-containing epidermal cells from the surface downward in a single pass
questions.exp: Solar lentigines are epidermal lesions (increased basilar melanocytes and melanin in basal/spinous layers). Q-switched 532 nm (green light — frequency-doubled Nd:YAG) is highly absorbed by epidermal melanin, producing reliable lentigo clearance in FST I–III, typically in 1–2 sessions. Ruby 694 nm also treats lentigines. Long-pulsed 1064 nm targets vascular structures, not epidermal melanin. Er:YAG ablates but leaves an open wound with higher scarring risk for flat lesions.

questions.q: Suction blister epidermal grafting for stable vitiligo uses negative pressure to create blisters at the dermoepidermal junction. The optimal pressure and duration for melanocyte-containing blister formation are:
opts: 100 mmHg for 30 minutes — rapid high-pressure technique for large-area donor harvest
400 mmHg for 20 minutes — high pressure rapidly detaches viable basal cell-containing epidermis
200 mmHg for 2–4 hours — slowly separates full-thickness epidermis including basal melanocytes from the dermis
150–200 mmHg for 1–3 hours — creates consistent blisters at the lamina lucida (DEJ), preserving basal layer melanocytes in the transferable epidermal graft roof
questions.exp: Suction blister grafting: 150–200 mmHg negative pressure for 1–3 hours creates subepidermal blisters at the lamina lucida — the weakest plane of the DEJ. The epidermal roof (containing viable basal melanocytes) is then transferred to the dermabrasion- or laser-ablated depigmented recipient site. It is the most minimally invasive surgical option for stable vitiligo (no new lesions ≥1 year). Colour match is excellent. Complications: donor site hyperpigmentation, cobblestone appearance if grafts are placed overlapping.

questions.q: Blunt-tipped microcannulas for HA filler injection are preferred over sharp needles in high-risk anatomical zones primarily because:
opts: Cannulas allow deeper placement in the subcutaneous plane that sharp needles cannot reliably access

Cannulas displace rather than penetrate vessels, nerves, and fibrous septa — significantly reducing intravascular injection risk, bruising, and nerve injury in high-risk zones compared to sharp needles
Cannulas provide better tactile feedback for detecting vessel wall resistance before accidental intravascular injection
Cannulas create less tissue trauma and allow faster injection with lower backpressure, reducing patient discomfort significantly
questions.exp: Blunt cannulas displace neurovascular structures laterally rather than penetrating them, dramatically reducing: (1) intravascular injection risk (most feared filler complication); (2) ecchymosis (fewer vessel perforations); (3) nerve injury. A single entry port serves a large area. Preferred high-risk zones: nasolabial folds, temples, nose, perioral, forehead. Disadvantages vs. sharp needles: less precise superficial placement, more force required, cannot be used for very superficial injections. Sharp needles remain preferred for fine work and the vermillion border.

questions.q: In photoaged skin, the primary molecular event driving dermal collagen degradation and wrinkle formation is:
opts: Decreased type IV collagen in the basement membrane zone causing progressive epidermal-dermal separation
Replacement of type I collagen by type III (fetal) collagen throughout the reticular dermis, reducing skin tensile strength

UV-driven activation of AP-1 transcription factor → upregulation of MMP-1 (collagenase) and MMP-3 → degradation of type I dermal collagen with accumulation of disorganised solar elastosis in the upper dermis
Loss of type II collagen from the dermal papillae, reducing papillary ridge support and causing epidermal flattening
questions.exp: UV radiation activates AP-1 (c-Fos/c-Jun heterodimer) transcription factor → upregulates MMP-1 (collagenase), MMP-3 (stromelysin), MMP-9 (gelatinase) → degrades type I and III collagens → disorganised, sparse collagen matrix. Simultaneously, UVA causes accumulation of abnormal elastin (solar elastosis) in the upper dermis. Type I collagen (90% of dermal collagen) loss is the primary structural change causing wrinkles. Tretinoin reverses photoageing by inhibiting AP-1 and upregulating procollagen.

questions.q: During cryotherapy for a seborrheic keratosis with liquid nitrogen, the clinical freeze endpoint for adequate treatment depth is:
opts: A 1–2 mm ice halo extending around the entire lesion base, with a freeze time of 5–10 seconds; two freeze-thaw cycles recommended for thicker hyperkeratotic lesions
Complete whitening of the lesion only (no perilesional halo) with a 30-second single freeze cycle for full-thickness destruction
Freeze until the lesion turns dark red-blue (cyanosis) indicating ischaemia of the full-thickness keratosis
Application until the patient reports intense burning pain, indicating adequate penetration to the dermoepidermal junction
questions.exp: For seborrheic keratosis, the cryotherapy endpoint is a 1–2 mm ice halo around the lesion base (ensuring full lateral and deep coverage), typically requiring 5–10 seconds with a spray or probe. One to two freeze-thaw cycles are used. Thicker hyperkeratotic lesions benefit from pre-treatment curettage and a second cycle. Over-aggressive freezing risks hypopigmentation or scarring; under-treatment risks incomplete removal and recurrence.

questions.q: For maximum follicular unit graft survival in hair transplant surgery, the most critical storage and timing factor between harvesting and implanting grafts is:
opts: Maintaining grafts at 37°C (body temperature) in isotonic saline to prevent hypothermic metabolic slowdown during the out-of-body period
Immediate implantation — all grafts must be placed within 30 minutes of harvesting to prevent ischaemic graft failure
Storage in antibiotic solution (gentamicin-saline) to prevent bacterial colonisation during the out-of-body period

Preventing desiccation by storing grafts in chilled (4°C) ATP-supplemented solution (HypoThermosol or saline) and implanting within 4–6 hours; time out of body >6 hours significantly reduces graft survival
questions.exp: Graft survival is critically dependent on preventing desiccation (even brief air exposure causes irreversible damage) and ischaemia. Best practice: store in chilled (4°C) saline or, preferably, HypoThermosol (organ preservation solution with ATP, antioxidants) — slows metabolic demand of follicular cells. Viability in chilled saline: 4–6 hours; HypoThermosol extends to 8–12 hours. Temperature above room temperature accelerates apoptosis. Grafts must never be allowed to dry out — the single most common preventable cause of graft failure.

questions.q: During an Nd:YAG 1064 nm laser procedure, protective eyewear for the operator and patient must have what minimum specification?
opts: OD ≥ 2 at 1064 nm — standard medical-grade eye protection for any wavelength above 400 nm
Wavelength-specific OD ≥ 4 at 1064 nm — attenuating the 1064 nm beam by 10⁴ (10,000×) to reduce transmitted energy below the retinal maximum permissible exposure (MPE)
OD ≥ 1 (90% attenuation) at any wavelength above 400 nm is sufficient for all medical laser procedures
Standard UV-blocking sunglasses (100% UV400) adequately protect against Nd:YAG 1064 nm since this is infrared, not UV radiation
questions.exp: Laser eye protection must be wavelength-specific (protect at the operating wavelength, not just UV) and of sufficient optical density. For Nd:YAG 1064 nm, minimum OD ≥ 4 is required — meaning the lens attenuates the beam by 10⁴ (0.01% of original intensity remains), keeping energy below the retinal MPE. Standard UV-blocking lenses are transparent at 1064 nm (near-infrared) and provide zero protection. Patients receive opaque metal corneal shields for periocular procedures.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman with a long history of tight braiding develops frontotemporal hair loss. Which finding best distinguishes traction alopecia from FFA on biopsy?
opts: Traction alopecia shows trichomalacia (distorted hair casts) and progressive perifollicular fibrosis WITHOUT perifollicular lymphocytic inflammation — unlike FFA which shows lichenoid (lymphoplasmacytic) infiltrate at the follicular isthmus; early traction alopecia is reversible
FFA shows neutrophilic infiltrate around follicles differentiating it from the lymphocytic infiltrate of traction alopecia
Traction alopecia shows exclamation mark hairs on biopsy confirming active peribulbar lymphocytic attack similar to alopecia areata
FFA and traction alopecia are histologically identical — they can only be differentiated clinically by the presence of eyebrow loss
questions.exp: Traction alopecia biopsy: early stages show trichomalacia (distorted, kinked hair casts from traction force) and normal or mildly inflamed follicles WITHOUT the perifollicular lichenoid lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate at the follicular isthmus seen in FFA. Chronic TA → perifollicular fibrosis but still lacks FFA's characteristic inflammation pattern. Early TA is reversible with hairstyle change; chronic TA produces permanent scarring. This biopsy distinction is important as both cause frontotemporal recession.

questions.q: Botulinum toxin for platysmal neck bands (Nefertiti lift): the correct injection technique and dose are:
opts: 5 U per band deep into the platysma at mid-neck level, 3–4 injection points per band
2–3 U per site injected subcutaneously (not intramuscularly) from mandible to clavicle along each visible band
2–5 U per injection point intramuscularly into visible bands every 1–2 cm along their length; total dose 20–60 U per session; injection too low risks dysphagia from spread to strap muscles
Single depot injection of 25 U at the widest point of each band, relying on toxin diffusion to distribute effects along the full band length
questions.exp: Platysmal band treatment: 2–5 U onabotulinumtoxinA injected into the muscle belly of each visible band at 1–2 cm intervals along its length, from mandible toward the clavicle. Total dose: 20–60 U depending on severity. Technique: grasp and pinch the band between fingers to avoid injecting deeper strap muscles. Complications: dysphagia, dysphonia, neck weakness from spread to sternohyoid/sternothyroid. The Nefertiti lift also includes along the inferior jawline to improve cervicomental angle.

questions.q: The most consistent histological feature of central centrifugal cicatricial alopecia (CCCA) that distinguishes it from other lymphocytic scarring alopecias is:
opts: Interface dermatitis at the follicular infundibulum with colloid (Civatte) bodies — identical to lichen planopilaris
Neutrophilic folliculitis with sinus tract and keloid formation — identical to folliculitis decalvans
Dense plasma cell infiltrate around the follicular isthmus with concentric lamellar fibrosis and lymphocytic satellites

Premature inner root sheath (IRS) desquamation causing perifollicular fibrosis with concentric lamellar collagen, and compound follicles (multiple hair shafts sharing one follicular infundibulum) as a diagnostic clue
questions.exp: CCCA histology is distinctive: premature IRS desquamation → hair shaft exposure to dermis → lymphoplasmacytic inflammation → concentric lamellar perifollicular fibrosis replacing the follicle. Compound follicles (2–3 hairs sharing one infundibulum) are characteristic and help differentiate CCCA from LPP/FFA. CCCA starts at the vertex and spreads centrifugally. FOXC1 and PADI3 variants implicated. Treatment: topical/intralesional corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, tetracyclines; avoidance of chemical relaxers.

questions.q: The nominal hazard zone (NHZ) in medical laser safety is defined as:
opts: The minimum distance from the laser aperture within which direct beam exposure always causes immediate irreversible retinal damage regardless of duration

The spatial zone within which direct, reflected, or scattered laser radiation exceeds the maximum permissible exposure (MPE) — where engineering controls, access restriction, and wavelength-specific protective eyewear are mandatory
The safe buffer zone outside which no protective measures are required regardless of laser power or exposure duration
The designated area immediately surrounding the patient being treated where the laser operator must stand during procedures
questions.exp: The NHZ is the zone around a laser system within which beam irradiance or radiant exposure exceeds the MPE for skin or eyes for the specific wavelength and exposure duration. Within the NHZ: engineering controls (interlocks, beam stops, warning signs), administrative controls (restricted access), and PPE (wavelength-specific OD-rated eyewear) are mandatory. Outside the NHZ, the beam has attenuated below MPE. NHZ dimensions are calculated from laser output, beam divergence, and wavelength-specific MPE values per ANSI Z136.1.

questions.q: Late-onset filler nodules (appearing months to years post-injection) suggest biofilm formation. The most appropriate initial management is:
opts: Empirical biofilm-active antibiotic therapy (e.g., clarithromycin 500 mg BD × 4–6 weeks) ± intralesional hyaluronidase if HA filler; avoid corticosteroids initially as they worsen biofilm infection
Immediate surgical excision of the nodule to prevent haematogenous bacterial seeding from the established biofilm
Intralesional triamcinolone 10 mg/mL as first-line — late filler nodules are always inflammatory granulomas that respond reliably to corticosteroids
Watchful waiting for 6–12 months — most biofilm-associated nodules resolve spontaneously without antibiotic treatment
questions.exp: Late nodules appearing months-years post-filler — especially triggered by dental work, URTI, or immunological challenge — suggest biofilm. Biofilm bacteria (S. epidermidis, atypical mycobacteria) resist standard short-course antibiotics and phagocytosis. Management: macrolide-based antibiotics (clarithromycin 500 mg BD × 4–6 weeks, with biofilm-disrupting properties) ± ciprofloxacin combination. If HA filler: hyaluronidase dissolves the filler scaffold. Corticosteroids worsen biofilm infection by immunosuppression and must be avoided until infection is excluded.
